intended_object: The graded (Koszul-signed) comparison map Dual M ⊗ Dual N → Dual(M ⊗ N) for ℤ-graded modules, given by (φ⊗ψ)(x⊗y) = (−1)^{|ψ||x|} φ(x)ψ(y), following the Getzler–Jones convention (from the docstring and module docs).
explanation: The body is Mathlib's dualDistrib followed by the dual of the Koszul twist automorphism, so w ↦ (z ↦ dualDistrib w (twist z)). The twist sends x⊗y (degrees p, q) to (−1)^{pq} x⊗y, giving (φ⊗ψ)(x⊗y) = (−1)^{pq} φ(x)ψ(y). In this library a functional ψ of degree r vanishes on every homogeneous piece except degree −r. So whenever ψ(y) ≠ 0 we have q = −|ψ|, and (−1)^{pq} = (−1)^{|ψ||x|}, the Getzler–Jones sign; otherwise both sides are 0. The library proves this as signedDualDistrib_tmul_tmul_of_mem_dualPiece. By linearity the definition agrees with the intended rule everywhere. It works over any commutative ring with no finiteness hypothesis; the ring must be commutative rather than a semiring because the sign needs negation. ℤ-grading is the standard setting for Koszul signs. Mathlib has only the unsigned TensorProduct.dualDistrib and no signed graded version.
